decision_reason: The legacy Forge URL redirects to the current INRAE Forge repository. The code has a direct GPL-3.0-only grant and is an actively maintained component of the live AgroMetInfo service, but it is expressly one component of the platform, requires season-core, and its own build/package instructions do not establish a separately installable user-facing product. Hold to avoid splitting the AgroMetInfo product family without evidence of independent use.

government_provenance.note: The official AgroMetInfo legal notice identifies INRAE as publisher, the head of its AgroClim service unit, and says its source code is published on the institute forge. The exact repository README identifies season-handler as an AgroMetInfo component.

public_source.note: The exact successor repository is publicly accessible on INRAE's official Forge and exposes the component source, README, license, and documentation without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The initial 2022 source commit contains the full GNU GPL version 3 text in License.txt; the README and Maven metadata refer to GPL version 3 without an explicit later-version option. Use GPL-3.0-only, not the broader metadata assertion GPL-3.0-or-later.

primary_evidence.note: The exact component documentation and current AgroMetInfo service confirm its operational role—launching SEASON calculations and handling their results—but do not establish separate adoption or a distinct product boundary from AgroMetInfo.

product_identity: season-handler, an internal Maven component that launches SEASON calculations and persists their results for the AgroMetInfo application
family_note: Treat as a component of the AgroMetInfo product family, not a second catalog product absent distinct reuse/adoption. Its README says it requires season-core and packages through Maven; it does not document an independently operated end-user service.
status_note: Current AgroMetInfo is an INRAE/AgroClim service. Official release notes expose current versions and SEASON functionality; source README describes this component. Source metadata's GPL-3.0-or-later assertion is broader than the directly inspected GPL v3 grant, so the conservative license wording is GPL-3.0-only.

decision_reason: This is the source for AgroMetInfo's user-facing map website, not a separate product from the live AgroMetInfo service. The application is maintained, documented, and directly GPL-3.0 licensed, but it should be represented with the complete AgroMetInfo family rather than as an additional standalone catalog identity.

government_provenance.note: INRAE is the official publisher of AgroMetInfo; the legal notice identifies the head of the AgroClim service unit and states that AgroMetInfo source code is on the INRAE forge. The exact repository README says this code is the map-displaying website component.

public_source.note: The exact successor repository is public on the INRAE Forge and contains the website application source, documentation, license, and publiccode metadata.

eligible_license.note: The dated source commit adds the full GNU GPL version 3 grant (License.txt); README names GPL Version 3. publiccode.yml claims GPL-3.0-or-later, but no direct later-version option was found, so record the source conservatively as GPL-3.0-only.

primary_evidence.note: The live official site identifies the interactive AgroMetInfo map and provides user instructions; the current service home lists a September 2026 release. This verifies operation of the sourced web app, though not an independent product separate from AgroMetInfo.

product_identity: AgroMetInfo web application/map interface (the public-facing web component of the AgroMetInfo service)
family_note: This is the AgroMetInfo user-facing website component and should not be listed as a second product alongside the full AgroMetInfo service. The component's publiccode metadata says standalone/web and GPL-3.0-or-later, but README and source grant identify it as the service website and only directly grant GPL Version 3.
status_note: The INRAE service is current, with public user help, release history, and source documentation. Earliest inspected grant-bearing source snapshot is 2023; the repository itself was created in August 2023. The product-family boundary, not freshness or live use, is why this URL is held.

decision_reason: The successor INRAE Forge repo is an actively maintained, independently deployable geographic-tile cache proxy with a direct GPL-3.0-only grant, versioned releases, and detailed installation/deployment instructions. Official AgroMetInfo release notes document its use in the agency's operational map service. This meets the agency-published reusable operational-tool pathway; catalog as the proxy server, not as AgroMetInfo itself.

government_provenance.note: The project is published in INRAE's AgroClim Forge namespace; the official AgroMetInfo legal notice identifies INRAE and the AgroClim service unit, and official AgroMetInfo release notes identify Tiles Proxy as a component used by that maintained service. Repository publiccode.yml identifies AgroClim as organization/usedBy and lists an INRAE maintainer contact; Cargo.toml itself does not carry an affiliation.

public_source.note: The canonical public INRAE Forge repo exposes Rust application source, README, Cargo manifest, configuration, deployment scripts, and license without credentials.

eligible_license.note: Cargo.toml explicitly declares GPL-3.0-only; the root LICENSE is the full GPL version 3 text and publiccode.yml agrees. Rust crate dependencies retain their own licenses and are not claimed to be covered by the root grant.

primary_evidence.note: Official AgroMetInfo release notes state that the service began using Tiles Proxy in its 2.0.0 alpha releases; the current service is live and maintained. The exact Tiles Proxy repo has v1.0.3 (2026-07-28) and README installation/deployment guidance for a standalone systemd service.

product_identity: Tiles Proxy, a standalone Rust cache proxy for geographic WMTS and XYZ tile servers
family_note: A distinct proxy service used within AgroMetInfo; do not merge its product identity into the AgroMetInfo website or application. Root GPL grant covers project-authored code; third-party Rust dependencies retain their own terms.
status_note: The 2024-03-27 initial commit contains the full GPL v3 text, Cargo.toml, and functional Rust source. Current Cargo metadata declares GPL-3.0-only. A 2026-07-28 commit versions 1.0.3; README describes installation, systemd service deployment, configuration, and redeployment. The source account's project metadata says stable and used by INRAE AgroClim; independent official service release notes confirm Tiles Proxy use.

decision_reason: COBY is an exact AnaEE France semantic-annotation pipeline with current official workshop use and public source. Its root LICENSE is GPL-2.0-only, but the repository still declares three code submodules pointing to the retired ForgeMIA host; their current source availability and license scope have not been reconciled. Hold until those dependencies are migrated or their applicable grants/materiality are verified.

government_provenance.note: The official AnaEE France 2026 workshop identifies COBY as an AnaEE-developed tool used for semantic annotation and in installation workshops. The exact repository is in AnaEE's INRAE Forge namespace.

public_source.note: The canonical repository is publicly accessible on the INRAE Forge with Java/Python pipeline source, documentation, root license, and submodule declarations. The three referenced submodule URLs remain on forgemia.inra.fr.

eligible_license.note: The top-level LICENSE is full GPL version 2 only. .gitmodules still points to yedgen, coreseinfer, and ontop-matarializer on the retired ForgeMIA host; their current contents and direct grants were not verified, so no product-wide license conclusion is safe.

primary_evidence.note: The official 2026 AnaEE France workshop says participants will use COBY for semantic annotation and describes the tool in a current training/workshop context, establishing exact-product use rather than merely an old catalog record.

product_identity: COBY, an AnaEE France pipeline that transforms relational/CSV data into RDF and supports semantic annotation
agency: AnaEE France national research infrastructure; project hosted by INRAE
license: GPL-2.0-only for the root repository; external submodule grants unresolved
family_note: This is an AnaEE data annotation pipeline rather than the unrelated commercial/product-intelligence service also named Coby. Do not extend the root GPL grant to submodule code until yedgen, coreseinfer, and ontop-matarializer are independently inspected.
status_note: The AnaEE event posted 2026-04-24 says the current workshop uses COBY for interoperability and semantic data annotation. The INRAE Forge repo's .gitmodules continues to reference the old ForgeMIA host. Although the root source is public and GPL-2.0-only, exact product-wide grant coverage and first licensed-source year are left unresolved pending dependency/license audit.

decision_reason: The exact repository grants CeCILL version 2.0, which is not an eligible OSI-approved version under the intake methodology (CeCILL 2.1 approval does not extend to 2.0). The project also has no current product-specific support/use signal after its last source activity in 2022. Reject on the confirmed license failure; a 2018 scientific paper and installation guide do not cure it.

government_provenance.note: The exact Family-Companion paper is listed on the official INRAE PlantBios publications page; the public project repository is under the BARIC namespace on the INRAE Forge, and paper authors include INRAE and CNRS researchers. This supports an INRAE research-project relationship, not a claim that every coauthor institution jointly owns the code.

public_source.note: The exact INRAE Forge repository is public and provides the web-server source, README with Docker/expert installation instructions, and a root license file.

eligible_license.note: The directly inspected license ends 'Version 2.0 dated 2006-09-05' and is CeCILL-2.0. It is not the OSI-approved CeCILL-2.1 version; no separate OSI-approved grant for the product source was found.

primary_evidence.note: The exact 2018 scholarly preprint describes Family-Companion as a web server and links source/installation instructions, but the Forge records last source activity in 2022 and no current product-specific service, supported release, or continued use was established.

product_identity: Family-Companion, a web server for computing, analyzing, visualizing, and sharing homology clusters
agency: INRAE BARIC research team; the exact product paper also lists CNRS researchers
license: CeCILL-2.0 (ineligible under the survey's OSI-license gate)
family_note: Catalog identity would be the Family-Companion research web server, not the generic homology-clustering methods or tools it wraps. The project is held back by the exact grant version and lack of current support/use; do not substitute CeCILL-2.1 eligibility for its actual CeCILL-2.0 text.
status_note: The INRAE project repository was created in 2020 after earlier project history imports; the direct license history includes an old 'Add license' commit, but the available record does not prove the date that this exact grant-bearing source first became publicly available.
